title: Every access to secret material produces a durable audit event
description: The Secrets Manager client emits a structured audit event on every fetch of a secret value: the logical name, the manifest path, the environment scope, the requesting principal (deployable name plus operator or agent id where applicable), the outcome (`served`, `refusedOutOfSlice`, `refusedAbsent`, `refusedRotationExpired`), and the wall-clock timestamp. The event never contains the secret value or any prefix or suffix of it. The audit sink is pluggable behind the same discipline as the wire log; the blueprint fixes the SHAPE of the events and the fields that must appear, not the storage engine.
rationale: Rotation, incident response, and least-privilege verification all depend on being able to answer 'who read what, when'. A missing audit trail is the difference between 'we know the blast radius' and 'we hope the blast radius is small'. Keeping the value out of the event is the discipline that makes shipping the audit stream to a third-party log store safe.
